provenance.paper_title: Learning Sensorimotor Primitives of Sequential Manipulation Tasks from Visual Demonstrations

latest_version.version_label: arXiv v1 / ICRA 2022 paper reviewed on 2026-08-31

representation_paths.memory_component: LSTM memory of completed tool-target-waypoint choices and manipulation subtasks

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. III Problem Formulation and Architecture
evidence.paraphrase: The paper states that the current 6-DoF object poses alone are insufficient because the robot must remember prior actions such as whether a brush was dipped. An LSTM compresses the history of selected tools, targets, and waypoints, and the high- and intermediate-level policies read this memory when choosing the next manipulation step.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. IV Learning from Visual Demonstrations
evidence.paraphrase: The memory output encodes which subtasks in the demonstrated sequence have already been performed. The memory-consistency and retrieval objectives train it to retain and recover earlier target, tool, and waypoint choices for later decisions.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. III Problem Formulation and Architecture; Sec. IV Learning from Visual Demonstrations
evidence.paraphrase: During a manipulation episode, the fixed learned LSTM update transforms the accumulated tool-target-waypoint history after each decision into a new persistent hidden state. Later policy decisions consume that changed state, while the update rule itself remains fixed.

adjudication_notes: The LSTM state is an explicit operative memory rather than ordinary stateless recurrence: the paper motivates it as necessary to remember completed subtasks and adds objectives for memory consistency and retrieval of earlier choices.

Tier T2 applies because the latent memory content changes within the deployed manipulation episode under a fixed learned update module. Training occurs before deployment, and no deployment-time feedback changes the update or retrieval policy, so T3 does not apply.
